patch.value: Historical program spine: the v1 delivery epoch is stored twice as disconnected roots, so no graph walk reaches the project's own origin

The tracker's first epoch is present but unreachable. Thirteen Epic items encode the original delivery programme twice — Milestone 0 through 6 (pm-2xl, pm-u9r, pm-c0r, pm-54d, pm-f45, pm-jiw) and PRD Milestone 0 through 6 (pm-6hhn, pm-zetb, pm-murz, pm-met4, pm-xtfo, pm-gyfn, pm-defw) — alongside pm-lty, the archived v1 build epic. All of them are parentless top-level roots with no edge to each other, no edge to the successor programme, and no ordering, so a traversal from today's roadmap terminates long before it reaches the work that produced v1. 184 terminal items carry no parent at all. The consequence is that every question of the form what preceded this, what did this epoch deliver, or how did the project get from its first milestone to its current outcome ladder is unanswerable by graph algorithm and answerable only by reading titles. The successor structure already exists and is well formed: pm-doxj indexes the post-v0.1 roadmap and six outcome milestones sit beneath it. What is missing is the join between the two eras and the internal ordering within the first one.

The duplicated milestone encoding is dispositioned explicitly as either two views of one programme or two distinct programmes, and the disposition is recorded on the items rather than inferred; The original milestones carry their delivery order as typed edges so a traversal can reconstruct the sequence without parsing titles; The v1 programme is joined to the post-v0.1 roadmap by a typed edge whose direction states which era succeeded which; Every parentless terminal item either gains a programme lineage or appears on a recorded residual list with the reason it has none; No item is retyped, renamed, or merged to achieve the join, and every edge added cites the durable evidence it came from; A graph query from the newest outcome milestone reaches the oldest v1 milestone, and the path is reported as evidence
Make the project's whole timeline a connected, ordered, typed graph from the first milestone to the current outcome ladder
Release archaeology, precedent retrieval, and long-horizon planning can all run as graph queries instead of manual reading
Every historical item gains a path to the programme that contained it, and the two eras become one traversable spine
One ordered v1 programme spine joined to the post-v0.1 roadmap, with the duplicate milestone encoding explicitly dispositioned rather than silently left as two roots
The terminal relationship backfill has just made every other closed item traversable, so the programme roots are now the only remaining discontinuity

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Resolved in substance 2026-07-27 by the epoch-lineage tranche recorded on pm-lnrk. The specific gap this item describes is closed: the thirteen duplicated v1 milestone Epics and the archived v1 build epic are no longer disconnected roots.

What was written for this item's scope specifically. The seven delivery Milestone epics now carry implements to their PRD counterparts, so the two encodings of the same programme are joined rather than parallel. All seven also carry implements to the canonical v1 build epic, giving the first epoch an internal hierarchy it never had. The canonical v1 build epic supersedes the archived duplicate, which was the one relationship the titles stated and the data did not. Every epoch root, including all fourteen named in this item's description, now carries blocks to the index root, so a traversal from today's roadmap reaches the project's origin.

Verified after the write: the workspace is a single connected component of 2,116 nodes with zero orphans, and every one of the 1,805 terminal items reaches the index root, against 820 before.

What is not closed by that tranche and should keep this item open or become its successor: the ordering between epochs is still derived at query time from creation timestamps rather than declared, so an epoch is not yet a first-class object with a start, an end and a stated successor. The description's framing of 184 parentless terminal items is also now stale — the count was 66 Epics plus 118 other types, and all 184 have lineage, but 70 of the 118 have only the weak precedes-the-index-root edge because no evidence supported a specific epoch. Those 70 are the honest residue.
